title: Microsoft SC-300 Identity and Access Administrator
shortTitle: Microsoft SC-300 Identity and Access Administrator
summary: Exam SC-300 is Microsoft's associate level certification for identity and access administrators, and passing it earns the Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator Associate title. It suits engineers who already work with Microsoft Entra ID, the cloud directory formerly named Azure Active Directory, and who now need to design, run and troubleshoot sign in, access and governance for a whole tenant. The exam mixes multiple choice questions with scenario based items, so it tests decisions rather than definitions. A pass signals to an employer that you can treat identity as a security control, and it supports roles such as identity administrator, cloud security engineer and IAM (Identity and Access Management) specialist. Microsoft revises the objective list from time to time, so confirm the current version before booking. This page is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with Microsoft.

beginner.definition: SC-300 is a Microsoft exam for people who manage identity and access in the cloud. The full title is Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator, and the exam code is SC-300. Identity means the accounts, groups and devices that a company chooses to trust. Access means the rules that decide what those accounts may open and when. Passing the exam earns an associate level certification.
beginner.whyItMatters: Identity is now the main door into most company systems, so employers pay for people who can protect it. This certification proves that you can set up sign in rules. It also shows that you can ask for stronger proof of identity. You can then give the right access to the right people. Many cloud security incidents begin with a stolen account, so this skill is in demand. The title also sits on a clear path towards the expert level Microsoft cybersecurity architect certification.
howItWorks: Study the four objective areas in order, because each one builds on the identity basics from the one before.
Use a free trial tenant as a laboratory. Create test users, groups and applications, then change the settings instead of only reading about them.
Write short notes for every feature you configure. Record the problem it solves and the case where you would not use it.
Practice scenario questions. The exam often gives a business requirement and asks which control fits best.
Revise the monitoring and reporting tasks last, because they tie the other three areas together.
Before you book, read the current objectives on Microsoft Learn and compare them with your own notes.
beginner.example: Imagine a company where staff sign in with only a password. One Friday an attacker steals a password with a phishing email and reads the finance mailbox. On Monday you change the rules. Staff must now approve each sign in on their phone. Anyone who opens finance files from an unknown country is blocked. You also add a monthly review so that managers confirm their team still needs each permission. Nothing in that story is complicated, but each step matches a task from the SC-300 objectives. The exam asks you to choose the right control for a situation like this one.
takeaways: SC-300 is an associate exam, so expect hands on configuration rather than simple definitions.
You need a test tenant, because reading alone will not teach you these settings.
Check the current objectives, because Microsoft updates this exam regularly.

objectives: Explain what the SC-300 certification proves and which roles it supports
Describe how Microsoft Entra ID stores and manages identities
Choose the right authentication control for a business requirement
Plan a study laboratory using a trial tenant
Tell the difference between access management and identity governance

chapters.title: Implement and manage user identities
objectives: Configure and manage built in and custom Microsoft Entra roles
Create, configure and manage users and groups in the tenant
Manage external users, cross tenant access settings and cross tenant synchronization
Implement hybrid identity with Microsoft Entra Connect Sync or Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
Manage password hash synchronization, pass through authentication and seamless single sign on
Manage custom security attributes, license assignment and device join settings

chapters.title: Implement authentication and access management
objectives: Plan and implement authentication methods such as Microsoft Authenticator, passkeys and temporary access passes
Configure tenant wide multifactor authentication and self service password reset
Design and build Conditional Access policies, including assignments, controls and session limits
Test and troubleshoot Conditional Access so that legitimate users are not blocked
Use Microsoft Entra ID Protection to find and remediate risky users and risky sign ins
Deploy Global Secure Access clients and profiles for private and internet access

chapters.title: Plan and implement workload identities
objectives: Choose between managed identities, service principals, user accounts and managed service accounts
Create a managed identity and assign it to an Azure resource
Integrate enterprise applications, including on premises apps through Microsoft Entra Application Proxy
Plan and create app registrations, app roles and API (Application Programming Interface) permissions
Manage user and admin consent, and configure application collections
Monitor application access with Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps

chapters.title: Plan and automate identity governance
objectives: Plan entitlement management with catalogs, access packages and connected organizations
Create and run access reviews, then act on the results
Manage privileged roles with Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management
Create and control emergency access accounts
Review sign in, audit and provisioning logs to investigate identity activity
Monitor the tenant with diagnostic settings, workbooks and Identity Secure Score
